newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ASTON VILLA AIM TO SCORE ON STOCK MARKET.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ASTON VILLA AIM TO SCORE ON STOCK MARKET.

text.p: English premier league club Aston Villa said on Thursday they planned to float on the London stock exchange in spring this year, joining the nation's growing league of listed soccer clubs.

"The commercial side of football is moving with terrific speed and we must therefore ensure we have every opportunity to continue to compete with the best in Europe, both on and off the field," Aston Villa chairman Doug Ellis said in a statement.

Britain's soccer sector has expanded strongly in recent years, leaving behind the hooligan-plagued 1980s to become a multi-million pound leisure industry keen to promote itself as family and business-oriented.
Eight of England's 20 premier league clubs are either listed or planning to float. The latest, Newcastle, are aiming to to join their ranks in spring.

Despite some hiccups, notably at second division Millwall which is fighting to put together a financial rescue package, shares in top sides Manchester United, Leeds and Tottenham have almost trebled over the past year, helped by lucrative television deals and merchandising.
The listings have enabled clubs to pump thousands of pounds into improving stadium facilities and to indulge in a global shopping spree to add foreign flair to the British leagues.

Critics of the newly-galvanised soccer sector argue the big clubs' march into big business could wreck the fortunes and lower league players. Many fear clubs could struggle to survive in the long term unless they join the race for new funds, a worry tacitly acknowledged by Villa's Ellis.
"I believe it is in the best long-term interests of the club to gain a listing at this time. Our 8,000 shareholders will also benefit from a more liquid market," he said.

Former European champions Villa said they would aim to raise between 15 and 20 million pounds ($24-32 million) in a share placing and an open offer. That would value the club at between 120 million and 140 million pounds, including the new money raised from the issue.
The Birmingham-based club said the funds would be used to improve their 39,400-seater Villa Park stadium and to provide working capital.
Villa said details of the flotation would be released in the near future.
